supports: waiting UPDATE reevaluates predicate against new row

sources.title: PostgreSQL 16 — UPDATE
supports: UPDATE 0 not being a SQL error

sources.title: PostgreSQL 16 — Monitoring Statistics
supports: separating actual wait from timing assumption

claims.statement: SELECT FOR UPDATE blocks another transaction from taking a conflicting row lock until the current transaction finishes.
claims.rationale: The official row-locking reference describes lock conflicts and transaction lifetime.

claims.statement: At READ COMMITTED a row-updating command can wait for a concurrent writer and reevaluate its WHERE clause on the newly updated version of the row.
claims.rationale: The isolation reference explicitly describes reevaluation of concurrent UPDATE conditions.

claims.statement: PostgreSQL UPDATE may affect zero rows without producing an SQL error, so a wallet debit must inspect affected-row count before recording a withdrawal.
claims.locator: UPDATE Outputs: UPDATE count and zero-row behavior
claims.rationale: The UPDATE command specification says UPDATE 0 is successful as a command.

claims.statement: Locking shared database objects in a consistent order reduces deadlock risk when opposing transactions touch the same set of accounts.
claims.rationale: The PostgreSQL documentation recommends consistent acquisition order.

claims.statement: SELECT supports an ORDER BY clause together with FOR UPDATE row locking, allowing an explicit account ID lock-order contract.
claims.locator: SELECT Syntax / ORDER BY and FOR UPDATE
claims.rationale: The SELECT reference defines both clauses in a single SELECT query.

claims.statement: The pg_stat_activity view exposes wait_event_type so a test can assert a session actually waits on a Lock event.
claims.rationale: The statistics reference documents activity and wait event fields.
